hallOfFame.name: Toad (Series 1, 2002)
hallOfFame.why: Last-minute Doctor Doom stand-in, shipped only in the initial assortment. The line's first grail.

reissueRadar.note: Short-packed in the initial assortment; rarity is structural, not availability-driven.

hallOfFame.name: Stealth Iron Man (Series 1 variant)
hallOfFame.why: Rare first-wave variant topping community rarest lists.

reissueRadar.note: Deco variant of a first-wave mold — a reissue would collapse the premium.

hallOfFame.why: Chase figure never pictured on the box back — the template for ML chase culture.

reissueRadar.note: True short-pack chase; Toy Biz-era chases were never reissued.

reissueRadar.note: HasLab Sentinel (2020) exists; availability-driven premium.

hallOfFame.name: Doomsday Wave 1 (2026) — the launch curve
hallOfFame.priceNote: Launch-curve case — reported solds, not a valuation. Gambit: $79.99 (Sep 24, 2026) → $25.99 presale (Oct 9, 2026), tracker avg $49.32. Cyclops: $64.99 (Sep 25) → $40.99–$52.99 (Oct 3–4).
hallOfFame.why: The sellout-spike-cool pattern, documented point by point: GamesRadar reported wave-1 Doom, Cyclops and Gambit selling out at retailers within hours of pre-orders opening (Aug 2026); actionfigure411 sold trackers then recorded the premium collapsing toward the $27.99 MSRP inside six weeks. The canonical example of why the Chronicle says: never pay the launch premium.

reissueRadar.note: The wave-1 premium was pure time-decay, not rarity — documented at $79.99 → $25.99 in 15 days. Availability premiums cool; this is the chart that proves it (launch-curve.html).

history.detail: Isaac Perlmutter's Toy Biz, successor to Charan/Chantex, holds the Marvel master toy license from 1990.
Marvel files for bankruptcy; Toy Biz merges with Marvel Entertainment Group to form Marvel Enterprises, Toy Biz becoming its toy division.

Marvel Legends launches as a Spider-Man Classics spin-off: clamshell packaging plus a 32-page reprint comic. Wave 1: Iron Man, Captain America, Hulk, Toad — aimed at adult collectors with best-in-class sculpt and articulation.
Series 9 (Galactus series) packs one piece of an 18" Galactus per figure — the Build-A-Figure is born. Followed by the Sentinel, Apocalypse, Giant-Man, Onslaught, Mojo and M.O.D.O.K.
Marvel terminates the Toy Biz Worldwide license a year early, paying a $13–16M penalty.
Marvel grants Hasbro a 5-year master toy license: $205M guaranteed royalties, $100M non-refundable advance. Retail sales begin Jan 1, 2007 with Ghost Rider and Spider-Man 3 lines.
New packaging drops the comic pack-in; new molds drop Toy Biz's signature finger joints. BAF continues with Annihilus, Brood Queen and others.
Announced at SDCC 2010 after fan demand and MCU momentum; all-new sculpts return January 2012.
Retooled as Marvel Legends: Infinite Series at $19.99 MSRP — box packaging, bigger BAFs, more accessories.
Photo-real face-printing for MCU likenesses; butterfly joints; pinless joints debut ~2020 and become standard.
First ML HasLab: 26.3" Sentinel at $349.99, funded in ~24 hours.
32" Galactus at $399.99 draws 14,000 backers — the biggest ML ever.
24" Giant-Man at $199.99 finishes with 13,876 backers. Ghost Rider's Engine of Vengeance becomes the line's only failed HasLab.
Standard MSRP reaches $24.99; deluxe $30–50; box sets $40–90; HasLab $200–400.

items.text: The line inherited clamshell packaging and a 32-page reprint comic from Toy Biz's Spider-Man Classics line. Wave 1 (Iron Man, Captain America, Hulk, Toad) shipped this way.

Each package included a display stand (wall-mountable for all but Toad's) and a comic reprinting a significant issue for that character. The box back listed the four figures with short bios — the gold-variant Iron Man was notably absent from the box back, an early example of variant omission.
International versions substituted posters for the 32-page comic pack-in.
UK and Canada releases are documented with "Gold Poster" pack-ins across Series 1–3 (e.g. Captain America w/ Gold Poster UK/CA).

sections.title: Hasbro takeover: the comic is dropped

items.text: Hasbro's packaging dropped the comic book pack-in; new molds also dropped Toy Biz's signature finger joints. The Build-A-Figure program continued.

The 2013/14 relaunch moved carded figures to a scooped-side window box format. The Winter Soldier wave (2014) featured blue highlight side art with the character name; the wave checklist and BAF info printed on the back.
The move also folded MCU characters into the main line rather than per-movie waves.

Hasbro removed plastic windows as part of a sustainability push; new boxes used printed images of the figure instead of a window, with comic-art-themed designs. Collector complaints centered on not being able to inspect the actual figure (figure-swapping risk). The Retro line and most Star Wars Vintage Collection were exempt.
Hasbro responded by commissioning real comic artists for box art: Ryan Stegman on the Venom: Separation Anxiety 3-pack; Dan Vessenmeyer on the X-Men: The Animated Series VHS-style boxes.

Following collector feedback, Hasbro announced the re-introduction of windows/blisters for 6-inch fan figures (Marvel Legends, Black Series, G.I. Joe Classified, Lightning Collection), made from bio-PET or recycled PET, rolling out late 2023 into 2024.
Marvel Legends 20th Anniversary (2022): premium updates of the 2002 Wave 1 characters (Cap, Iron Man, Hulk, Toad) in retro-style packaging, sold as Fan Channel exclusives.
Spider-Man: The Animated Series retro cards (2023): figures on Toy Biz 1990s-style cardbacks; sold via Entertainment Earth, BBTS, Zavvi UK/US/CA, and Amazon at $24.99–$25.99.

Iron Man animated retro wave (revealed at WonderCon): Model 9, Model 20, Model 1 (gold repaint), Count Nefaria, comic Whiplash, and on-model She-Hulk — an homage to the 90s Toy Biz Iron Man cartoon line (whose vac-metalized interchangeable armor Hasbro did not reproduce).
Maximum Carnage packaging homage: the 90s video-game/comic packaging recreated for a Retro Spider-Man Carnage reissue — "a delight for packaged collectors."

The X-Men '97 mainline wave (pre-order Oct 21, 2026) and the Spider-Man: The Animated Series wave (pre-order Sep 29, 2026) both ship on retro blister cards — the 2026 packaging story is nostalgia cards, not a new overhaul.
items.source: Mephitsu — NYCC 2026 Hasbro Marvel Legends panel (Oct 10, 2026)

items.text: Mini Comics Wave 3 (pre-order Oct 6, 2026) revives a pack-in for the first time since the Hasbro takeover: every figure ships with a physical mini comic, a replica of its source issue's cover (e.g. Hawkeye #3, 2012 for the Fraction/Aja Hawkeye).

Retro cards also carry the 2026 reissues of previously Pulse-VHS-exclusive Spider-Man: TAS figures (Mary Jane, Aunt May, Smythe, Carnage) — the packaging change is part of Hasbro's aftermarket-cooling reissue program.

No new major packaging overhaul in 2025–2026: the 2022–23 plastic-free experiment was reversed in April 2023 (bioPET/recycled PET windows back for all 6" fan lines, see 'Windows return' above), and 2026 builds on that base. (Absence of evidence, single-source — no overhaul announcement found.)

sections.title: Deco vs. sculpt vs. packaging vs. label

items.text: Deco variants (repaints) are the dominant modern chase form. Example: the ML1 Iron Man mold reused as gold armor with horned face mask, Walmart-exclusive Stealth Iron Man, Silver Centurion, and War Machine — same sculpt, different deco. The ML1 Iron Man was sculpted by Dave Cortez.
Sculpt variants are rarer and more valuable — e.g. Weapon X Wolverine vs. Damaged Weapon X (Giant Man series, Toy Biz), distinct sculpts.
Label variants: Stealth Iron Man exists with and without "Stealth" on the package label.
First Appearance variants: Iron Man First Appearance in gold and grey deco variants (2002/2005).

Packaging variants: same figure, different card — e.g. the Gold Poster UK/CA releases, and modern Retro-carded reissues of existing sculpts (Spider-Man: The Animated Series cards, Maximum Carnage packaging).

Collector guidance (Chronicle analysis): deco variants — buy the look you like; premiums fade on reissue. Sculpt variants and true short-packs (1× per case or revision-only) hold value better. Packaging variants matter mainly to carded collectors. Unreleased prototypes: verify provenance before believing any price.

Marvel Legends "initially used the 'chase' concept to introduce figures based on less popular characters," shipping them in fewer quantities; over time the concept evolved into variants (alternate head or deco) of a same-series figure, which stayed sought-after.
Case ratios are set by the assortment number printed on the shipping case, not by the wave. One wave can span multiple assortments, and "revision cases" swap variants in/out mid-wave.

Modern standard case: 8 figures. Examples from retailer listings: X-Men Wave 1 (Ch'od BAF) — 2× Cyclops, 1× each of Fang, Monet, Corsair, Kid Omega, Chamber, Emma Frost; Super Villains Wave 1 (Xemnu BAF) — 2× Dr. Doom, 1× each of 6 others; Cassie Lang wave — 2× Ant-Man, 1× each of 6 others; Gilgamesh wave — 2× Ikaris, 1× each of 6 others. Retailer mixes are "subject to change."
items.source: Entertainment Earth / ActivePowerSports / BBCW (primary retail data)

items.text: Historical: the 2007 Brood Queen wave shipped an initial case (1× Bucky, 1× each of Cap, Marvel Girl, Hydra Soldier, Colossus, Cyclops, Danger, Black Knight) and a "revision" case adding the Marvel Girl variant and Hydra Soldier variant at 1× each; BBTS sold a dedicated variant case.

2006 MODOK series: collectors debated whether its Wasp variants (black/red/blue), Moon Knights, Spider-Women, and Destroyer-as-Thorbuster were packed 1-per-case. No authoritative ratio was ever published — treat 1-per-case claims as rumor.
Hasbro prints 5-digit SKU codes on figures (G/F prefix in recent years; older were all-numeric). The code matches the product number on the cardback; older QA/batch codes also appear on legs/feet.
For Target exclusives, collectors use Target DCPIs (internal item numbers) to locate stock via scanners and employee pulls.

Practical rule (collector consensus): a figure is a "chase" if it appears 1× per case while the rest are 1–2×, or only in revision assortments. No official "chase ratio" is published by Hasbro — all ratios are reverse-engineered from case mixes.
items.source: Negative claim verified across all sources above

items.text: SDCC 2007: She-Hulk + Stan Lee — Hasbro's first ML SDCC exclusive.
SDCC 2008: Savage Land 3-pack (Ka-Zar, Shanna, Zabu).
SDCC 2012: Uncanny X-Force 3-pack (Archangel, Wolverine, Psylocke; Clayton Crain box art) — $49.99 retail; "insanely hard to acquire."
SDCC 2013: Thunderbolts 5-pack — $89.99 at booth; $130–$300 sold later.
SDCC 2014: Thanos Imperative set.
SDCC 2018: Red Skull with Tesseract; Defenders box set.
SDCC 2024: X-Men arcade Sentinels; Kang the Conqueror — shown at SDCC as PulseCon exclusives.
SDCC 2026: Professor X & Hoverchair (X-Men '97); Spider-Man 60s cartoon 3-pack (Spider-Man, Lizard, Electro; $84.99) — booth first, then Hasbro Pulse online.

Pattern (verified across 2024/2026 coverage): modern SDCC exclusives are booth-first, then Hasbro Pulse online — genuinely limited at the show but given a wider online release, which tempers aftermarket spikes.
PulseCon 2020: Hellfire Club box set + Hellfire Club Guard ($14.99) army-builder; Silk (2020 Fan Vote winner, $19.99).
PulseCon 2021: retro-carded Venom ($31.99) and M.O.D.O.K. World Domination Tour set ($73.99, with The Captain) — Pulse exclusive in US/Canada/UK.

Target: Hasbro Wave 7 was the Red Hulk Series, a Target-exclusive wave. The modern program runs through Target Geek-Out/Geek Fest events: 2026 brought a No Way Home "Final Swing" Spider-Man ($27.99) and the first-ever Cypher figure; X-Men Onslaught ($39.99) was "extremely hit or miss in stores." Target also cancelled many confirmed 2026 preorders, angering collectors.
items.source: Marvel Toys Wiki / Marvel Toy News / Bleeding Cool

items.text: Walmart: Toy Biz Giant Man Series was a Walmart exclusive; Hasbro Ares and Nemesis BAF waves were Walmart-exclusive waves. Modern: Walmart Collector Con events — 2026 brought Avengers: Doomsday FF figures (Mister Fantastic + H.E.R.B.I.E. $39.97; Invisible Woman + Human Torch $55; The Thing $69.95).

Walgreens became the de facto Fantastic Four/Inhumans destination — Invisible Woman (2017), Human Torch, Mr. Fantastic, Thing, Namor, Medusa, Silver Surfer, Quasar, Binary, Sentry, Baron Zemo (Thunderbolts). The Fwoosh called it "the church of Marvel Legends." Limited store quantities; many also sold on walgreens.com.
Toys'R'Us (defunct): Emma Frost (Diamond) 2007, Black Queen 2007, Valkyrie 2010; TRU variant 2-pack Black Widow + Winter Soldier (comic-costume variant).
Amazon: 2025 Marvel vs. Capcom box sets — Wolverine vs. Silver Samurai, Psylocke vs. Thanos (Target), War Machine vs. Omega Red (Walmart), Shuma-Gorath/Gargantos, Juggernaut.
Previews (comic shops): Wolverine (Ultimate) 2008, Sunfire (Age of Apocalypse) 2008 Fan's Choice.
Fan Channel (online specialty retailers): 20th Anniversary line (2022), Malice, Rictor/Domino/Cannonball X-Force 3-pack reissues.

Truly limited vs. widely restocked (Chronicle analysis): truly limited — SDCC booth quantities before the Pulse online release, the 2012 X-Force and 2013 Thunderbolts con sets (both carry verified aftermarket premiums), and the Toy Biz Walmart Giant Man series. Restocked — the X-Force 3-pack and Retro Animated Spider-Man got Fan Channel reissues in 2026; Target Onslaught restocked sporadically. Rule of thumb: Pulse-era (2020+) exclusives are produced to meet demand and often return; pre-2020 con exclusives generally were not.
Toy Biz-era international releases substituted posters for the 32-page comic pack-in; UK and Canada additionally got documented "Gold Poster" variants across Series 1–3.

UK Tesco re-issues: a wave of MCU figure re-issues appeared at Tesco UK in basic cardback packaging with no BAF pieces — a stripped-down international assortment (Spider-Man FFH, Stealth Suit, Endgame Cap, IW Iron Man, IW Black Panther).
Disney Stores UK: the Avengers 5-pack (Thor, Hulk, Iron Man, Cap, Ultron) at £99.95 was a European/UK exclusive.
Hasbro product data sheets list EUROPE / AMERICAS packaging regions, confirming distinct regional packaging runs (e.g. Icecat product data for The Spot, G08305L0).
PulseCon exclusives (e.g. the 2021 Venom) were sold on Hasbro Pulse in the US, Canada & UK.
UK sellers (e.g. BigBrandToys) actively trade Toy Biz variants like the Series 1 Stealth Iron Man, indicating healthy UK collector circulation of US releases.
Research gap: no authoritative source was found for dedicated Asian-market Marvel Legends variants; most "international" product is US product with regional packaging. Do not invent any.

AFA (Action Figure Authority) now operates as a division of Collectible Grading Authority (CGA), Roswell, Georgia. On Sept 22, 2026 CGA opened a New York drop-off office (grading still performed in Georgia). Tom Derby (founder, ex-Cloud City Collectibles) is a Partner at CGA. CGA also runs VGA (video games) and MGA (media, newly launched); it claims 25+ years via AFA/VGA.

Scale: 0–100 in increments of 5; the modern scale is the original ÷ 10 (85 = 8.5). Sub-grades: card (C), blister/bubble (B), figure (F). "Y" = yellowed bubble. "U" = uncirculated (submitted in a sealed factory case — divisive; critics call it destroying a vintage item to preserve it).

Historic costs (dated forum anecdotes — verify current before relying on them): ~$16 standard / $28 express (3-day) per jedidefender.com (old); ~$45+ with shipping for a modern figure (2008 forum); up to ~$90–100 all-in for large items (2012 forum). Turnaround 30–40 working days on the cheapest tier (old). No current CGA price list was found.
AFA trains graders to reject recards, reseals, and repros; forum anecdotes allege fakes have been graded — contested.
Independent grading/authentication (collectorarchive.com). Anti-"U"-grade stance; offers a "preservation grade" for damaged-but-rare items.
Nov 17, 2025: BigBadToyStore partnered with CAS — sells CAS Graded & Cased items with tamper-proof acrylic blocking up to 85% UV and a digital certificate per item.
Cost anecdote: ~$100 all-in including return shipping for one baggie figure; turnaround quoted ~90 days, actual ~4 months (2023–24).
UK-based grader; ~£23–26 per MOC all-in (2012-era anecdote); grades like Y85; known for fast personal communication.
TGA (tgacards.com): "Due to slow sales... TGA is no longer accepting submissions." Do not send figures there.

sections.title: Do graded Legends sell at premiums?

items.text: No Marvel-Legends-specific graded-vs-ungraded sale premium was found in any source. One Star Wars forum anecdote claims graded items change hands for 1/3 to 2× ungraded; a counter-anecdote (UKG thread) reports graded MOCs resold for less than the pre-grading purchase price.

The Chronicle will NOT claim a grading premium for Marvel Legends — no documented Legends-specific evidence exists. Present grading as authentication + preservation + buyer confidence, with any premium unproven.

priceMethod.principle: Sold listings, not active listings. Active listings show what sellers hope to get; sold/completed listings show what buyers actually paid.
principleSources: The Spruce Crafts — Guide to Pricing Action Figures (https://www.thesprucecrafts.com/guide-to-pricing-action-figures-17887)
steps: eBay → advanced search → SOLD listings, last 90 days.
Filter to your exact condition tier: loose complete / boxed / graded.
Take the median of the last 10–15 solds, drop outliers.
Asking prices are irrelevant — only solds count.
rules: Every price carries: amount, condition tier, source, date observed.
"Asking" vs "sold" is labeled every time — never mixed.
No price presented as current without an observation date.

reissueEffect.mechanism: Reissue announced → speculative listings undercut each other → asking prices fall within days. Originals keep a premium only when the value driver is rarity/provenance (prototypes, true limited runs), not mere availability.

cases.detail: Aftermarket was "escalating quite a bit" on sold-out Pulse VHS Animated Series exclusives (MarvelToyNews) → Hasbro reissued four (Mary Jane, Aunt May, Smythe, Maximum Carnage) on Retro cards at $27.99. Clean documented sellout → spike → reissue. Before/after price numbers were not published.
"Back by popular demand... previously an exclusive," reissued at $46.99–$47.99.
A $250 listing met a reissue announcement (ToyFarce satire — documents sentiment, not a transaction).
"A middling seller, lingering on store shelves" (comicbook.com). Rarity-based grails (~10 known prototypes) are immune to reissues; demand-based premiums are not.

honestGaps: No Marvel-Legends-specific graded-vs-ungraded sale premium found.
No current AFA/CGA price list found (only historic forum figures).
No before/after price numbers for the VHS → Retro reissues (spike documented, figures not published).
No exact production numbers for any Toy Biz chase variant ("~10 known" Blue Wasp is comicbook.com's estimate).
The rarest.org "$15,000 eBay sale" Blue Wasp claim is a single rarity-list anecdote.
